subject: Feature enablement onboarding: streaming + tool-calls + structured outputs
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@cardioapp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalls + structured outputs

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with Redwood for a real-time patient-summary feature that requires: streaming text responses, function/tool calling for medication lookup and charting, and a strict JSON schema for downstream ingestion into our analytics pipeline.

Can you share a sample onboarding plan and what technical artifacts you need from us to get started? We expect to be in pilot in ~3 weeks.

Attachments: none yet.

—Sara
Sara Liu
Head of Integrations, CardioApp
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@cardioapp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalls + structured outputs

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the clear ask. I put together a concise onboarding checklist and proposed MAP (mutual action plan) to hit pilot in 3 weeks. High level:

- Week 0: Kickoff + API key exchange + security questionnaire items (we only need a short subset to start)
- Week 1: Schema alignment & tool-call inventory (you send sample payloads and a list of external services the model should call)
- Week 2: Integration sprint — streaming endpoints + function wiring + structured-output validation
- Week 3: Canary pilot, quality checks, and handoff to CS/SE for monitoring

I attached our onboarding checklist (redwood_onboarding_checklist.xlsx). Can you share the sample JSON you expect for downstream ingestion and any hard SLOs for token-latency? Also, who will own the clinical tool-call contract at CardioApp?

Proposed kickoff: Wed Apr 7, 10:00 AM PT — 30m. If that works, I will send a calendar invite and a short MS Teams link.

Attachments: redwood_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

Best,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalls + structured outputs (internal prep)

Rishi / Laura —

Quick internal notes before kickoff:

- Streaming: confirm expected max tokens per session and avg chunk size. If they do ~1k tokens bursts we should pin batching window to 30ms to keep latency tight.
- Tool-calls: need a list of function signatures (name, input schema, expected outputs). We should recommend the function-call pattern that returns a tuple: {status, payload, diagnostics}.
- Structured outputs: propose we provide a validation hook in the SDK that runs their JSON Schema (we can host the validator in the private lane if they prefer).
- Security: ask for ACL owners and whether they require VPC/private deployment for pilot.

I'll draft a minimal JSON schema template and attach it to the thread once I have the first pass. Laura — can you review the quantization profile recommendation for their NLU workload?

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@cardioapp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalls + structured outputs

Thanks — attached is a sample payload our analytics team provided (cardioapp_sample_schema_v1.json).

Also: our tool inventory currently includes: medication-service@cardioapp.com (lookup), charting-service@cardioapp.com (append-only), and a secure patient-metadata service that will require an allowlist. All of those can be called via internal VPC endpoints; we can provide a test sandbox.

We do have a 200ms 95th-percentile requirement for the live patient-summary response after function calls complete. Let us know if that aligns with Redwood's suggested canary.

Attachment: cardioapp_sample_schema_v1.json

—Sara
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@cardioapp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalls + structured outputs

Sara —

Thanks for the sample schema and inventory. Quick answers / plan:

- Latency: 200ms p95 is achievable for the streaming response + one function call if we (a) pre-warm a dedicated worker for the pilot and (b) use prefix caching for common prompts. We'll propose a Dedicated burst config for the first 2 weeks of pilot.
- Tool-call pattern: we'll implement an async function-call helper that returns a function token and then streams the model output while awaiting the function result; we call your medication-service and charting-service using the VPC tunnel you provide.
- Schema validation: Monica will provide a draft JSON Schema validator hook. We can also surface schema regression alerts in Redwood Console and tie them to your evals set.

Next steps I will action today:
1) Send calendar invite for Apr 7 kickoff (10:00 AM PT)
2) Share a short SOW for signatures (handing you CardioApp_SOW_v1.pdf via DocuSign)
3) Provision a pilot key and a dedicated GPU worker for the first 10 days

DocuSign link: https://redwood.app/docusign/packet/23b7c1
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-4823

If that looks good we'll go live with the kickoff invite.

Best,
Rishi
